Database restores are notorious for requiring the same major version from which the backup originated. Especially when using binary formats for the backup.

@NoisyCricket has the right answer but your confusion as to why it isn't working with the new 2017 version is because you updated SSMS not SQL Server itself. The version of SSMS is a lot less critical to the backup/restore process than the database engine version. The reason you can't restore this backup is because it was created by the 2016 version of the SQL Server database engine and you are trying to restore it on the 2012 version of the SQL Server database engine. You upgraded the management tool (SSMS) but the database engine is still the same 2012 version (version 11). If this database backup is not too large, you can download the latest version of SQL Server Express and install it on a different machine so you can restore the backup file. According to Microsoft, the 2017 version of SQL Server Express has a 10GB maximum database size limitation (because it's free). If your backup is smaller than 10GB in its expanded form, then you can use Express to get your data.

Another alternative, which I have no direct experience with but will throw in as an option, is a product from Idera called SQLSafe (I have no affiliation with them). This tool will let you attach to a .bak file and use it like a virtual database, or so they claim, so you can recover your data without a true restore. The product has a 14 day free trial and claims to be fully functional during the trial period so maybe this will work if the above option of SQL Server Express doesn't pan out. I've used other Idera tools but not this one so I make no guarantees on its usefulness or safety.
